# $\mathbb Z_p$ inside a compact torsion-free group

Let $K\ne1$ be a compact Hausdorff topological group with no element of finite order other than $1$. Then for some prime $p$ there is a continuous injective homomorphism from the additive group $\mathbb Z_p$ to $K$.

**Remark (not formalized).** This is an open statement: the Lean states it now and proves it later. Planned route. Take $g\ne1$ in $K$. The closure $A$ of the subgroup generated by $g$ is a compact Hausdorff commutative subgroup, nontrivial and with no nontrivial element of finite order, and [the abelian case](zp-in-compact-abelian.md) applied to $A$ gives the homomorphism. The abelian case is itself proved from two open statements on characters, so this route closes only when those are proved.

**Remark (not formalized).** The construction gives more: with $x$ the image of $1$, the homomorphism extends $m\mapsto x^m$, and its image is the closure of the subgroup generated by $x$.
